info.title: CueRCode API
info.description:
REST API for generating, customising, and downloading QR codes. The CueRCode web UI is built ON TOP OF this API, so the API is the contract and the UI is just one client: every feature available in the UI is available here.

The API supports 26 QR code types and multiple output formats (PNG, JPG, GIF, WebP, SVG, PDF), custom colours and gradients, module and finder-pattern (marker) shapes, logo overlays, decorative frames with labels, error-correction selection, sizing, and an optional quiet zone.

## Authentication

The API supports two authentication methods (either satisfies a protected endpoint):

1. **API Key** - Include your API key in the `X-API-Key` header. Format: `cuercode_` followed by 40 hexadecimal characters. Obtain one from the admin panel.
2. **CSRF Token** - For web UI AJAX requests, include the session CSRF token in the `X-CSRF-Token` header.

Protected endpoints (`/generate`, `/preview`, `/download/{uuid}`, `/save`, `/qrcodes`, `/qrcodes/{uuid}`) require ONE of the above. Anonymous endpoints (`/bulk-generate`, `/types`, `/formats`, `/health`) require no authentication but are still rate limited.

## Saved-Codes Library (Epic E3 stage 2a)

`POST /save` claims a previously-generated QR code (by its `uuid`) into the authenticated caller's account, subject to the caller's plan `saved_codes` limit (`402 SAVED_CODES_LIMIT_REACHED` at/over the cap). `GET /qrcodes` lists ONLY the caller's own saved codes (paginated, optionally filtered by `type`). `GET/PATCH/DELETE /qrcodes/{uuid}` operate on a single saved code: ownership is re-checked on every request from the caller's authenticated identity, never from a client-supplied field. A code that is neither owned by the caller nor marked `is_public` is reported as `404` (never `403`) to avoid disclosing that a private UUID belonging to someone else exists. `DELETE` soft-deletes (frees a `saved_codes` slot; the row is retained for audit purposes). `is_public: true` (opt-in; default `false`) grants read/download access to any authenticated caller but never write access - only the owner may `PATCH`/`DELETE`.

## Self-Service API Keys & Scopes (Epic E7 stage 1, #54)

Authenticated users (session/CSRF only - see below) can self-service manage their own API keys under `/keys`. `POST /keys` creates a key (caller-chosen `name` + an optional `scopes` array from the allowlist below) subject to the caller's plan `api_keys` cap (`402 API_KEY_LIMIT_REACHED` at/over the cap) and returns the FULL raw key EXACTLY ONCE in the response body (`data.api_key`) - it is never retrievable again, only its HMAC-SHA256 hash is stored. `GET /keys` lists ONLY the caller's own keys (id, prefix, name, scopes, rate limits, `is_active`, `last_used_at`, `created_at`, `expires_at` - NEVER the secret or its hash). `POST /keys/{id}/rotate` issues a NEW secret for a key the caller OWNS (returned once, exactly like create) and immediately invalidates the old one; `DELETE /keys/{id}` soft-revokes (`isActive = 0`) a key the caller OWNS. Every `{id}` operation re-derives the caller's identity server-side and re-checks ownership in the same query as any mutation - a key that is not owned by the caller (or does not exist) is reported as `404` (never `403`, avoiding existence disclosure).

**Owner/design decision:** an X-API-Key-authenticated request to ANY `/keys*` endpoint is refused with `403 API_KEY_MANAGEMENT_FORBIDDEN`, regardless of that key's own scopes - only a CSRF/session-authenticated caller (the account dashboard) may create/list/rotate/revoke keys. This closes a self-escalation path: without it, a compromised low-scope key (e.g. only `generate`) could mint itself a brand-new key with EVERY scope.

**Scope allowlist:** `generate`, `preview`, `download`, `bulk`, `qrcodes:read`, `qrcodes:write`, `save`. A key with no scopes granted can authenticate but cannot access any scoped endpoint. Every scoped endpoint below documents its `requiredScope` in its own description. Scope enforcement applies ONLY to `X-API-Key` authentication - a session/CSRF-authenticated web UI request is NEVER scope-limited (full user rights). A key missing a route's required scope gets `403 INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE`, with the missing scope named in both the `message` and a `required_scope` field alongside the standard error shape.

## Rate Limiting

All endpoints, including `/health`, are rate limited by the same per-key/per-IP mechanism (no route is exempt). Rate limit headers are included on every rate-limited response:
- `X-RateLimit-Limit` - Maximum requests per minute
- `X-RateLimit-Remaining` - Remaining requests in the current window
- `X-RateLimit-Reset` - Unix epoch time (seconds) at which the window resets
- `Retry-After` - Seconds to wait before retrying (only on `429`)

## Request Body

POST request bodies must be sent with `Content-Type: application/json` (an optional charset parameter such as `; charset=utf-8` is permitted); otherwise the API responds with `415 Unsupported Media Type`. Request bodies larger than the configured maximum (256 KiB by default) are rejected with `413 Payload Too Large`. Per-field length caps also apply (type ≤ 64 chars, each input scalar ≤ 4096 chars, frame_label ≤ 120 chars) and over-long fields are rejected with `400 FIELD_TOO_LONG`.

## Response Format

By default, responses are in JSON. To receive XML instead, either:
- Set the `Accept` header to `application/xml`, or
- Add `?format=xml` to the query string.

XML responses share the same logical structure as JSON: a root `<response>` element wrapping `success`, `message`, `data`, optional `error_code`, and `timestamp`. Arrays serialise as repeated `<item>` elements.

## Output Formats

Supported formats: **PNG**, **JPG/JPEG**, **GIF**, **WebP**, **SVG**, and **PDF**. SVG additionally supports gradients and the extended (SVG-only) module/marker shapes; PDF is vector-only and does not support transparency, logo overlay, or frames.

**JPEG-XL (`jxl`) host limitation:** although the underlying schema reserves a `jxl` format value and the web server advertises the `image/jxl` MIME type, JPEG-XL is NOT an accepted `format` value on this deployment. The QR generation library / GD build on the Dreamhost host does not encode JPEG-XL, so requests asking for `jxl` are coerced to `png`. Use one of the six supported formats above.

post.summary: Bulk generate QR codes (ZIP, or an Avery label-sheet PDF)
post.description:
Generate many QR codes in a single synchronous request and receive them as a ZIP archive (`application/zip`). This endpoint is anonymous-capable (no authentication required) but is rate limited and subject to the same request-body-size cap as the other POST endpoints.

Provide EITHER an `items` array OR a `csv` string. An optional request-level `customization` object supplies shared defaults that each item's own customization overrides key-by-key.

The maximum number of items per request depends on the caller's subscription plan (`bulk_batch_size` limit, Epic E4) — anonymous callers get the `anonymous` plan's allowance (25 by default), while an authenticated user or API key resolves their own plan's allowance instead; exceeding it returns `413` with an `upgrade_url` hint. Per-item failures do NOT abort the batch — each item's outcome is recorded in a `manifest.txt` file inside the ZIP, and successfully generated images are named `NNN-<type>.<ext>`.

If the server's PHP `zip` extension is not installed, the endpoint returns `501 Not Implemented`.

**Avery label-sheet PDF (E5 / #49):** when the REQUEST-LEVEL (shared) `customization` sets `format: pdf` and `pdf_layout` to `avery_5160` or `avery_l7160`, the response is a DIFFERENT shape entirely — a single combined `application/pdf` Avery label-sheet document (not a ZIP) with each item tiled into successive label slots, spanning extra sheet pages as needed. Per-item `pdf_layout`/`format` overrides are ignored in this mode (every item is forced onto the same sheet layout — a mixed-layout sheet is not a coherent single PDF); per-item failures leave that label slot blank rather than aborting the sheet. See the Customization `pdf_layout` field for the full enum.

requiredScope: `bulk` — only enforced if the caller VOLUNTARILY supplies an `X-API-Key` on this anonymous-capable endpoint; a genuinely anonymous request never reaches the scope check at all.

items_array.summary: Explicit item list with shared defaults

200.description: ZIP archive of generated QR codes (plus manifest.txt) — OR, when the shared customization requests `format: pdf` with `pdf_layout: avery_5160`/`avery_l7160` (E5 / #49), a single combined Avery label-sheet `application/pdf` document instead. See the operation description.

Content-Disposition.description: Attachment filename for download (`cuercode-bulk.zip`, or `cuercode-bulk-avery_5160.pdf`/`cuercode-bulk-avery_l7160.pdf` for the Avery-sheet response)

X-Bulk-Failed.description: Number of items that failed (see manifest.txt, or left blank on the Avery sheet)

application/pdf.description: Returned instead of application/zip when pdf_layout is avery_5160/avery_l7160 (E5 / #49).

get.description:
Download a previously generated QR code file by its UUID. The file is returned with the correct Content-Type header and a Content-Disposition header that triggers a browser download.

Requires authentication (API key OR CSRF token). requiredScope: `download` (API-key requests only; session/CSRF requests are never scope-limited).

**Owner-or-public access rule:** an UNCLAIMED (never `POST /save`d) code is downloadable by any authenticated caller. A CLAIMED code that is not marked `is_public` is downloadable ONLY by its owner. A CLAIMED code marked `is_public: true` is downloadable by any authenticated caller. In every denial case the response is an IDENTICAL `404 NOT_FOUND` (never `403`) - this is a deliberate anti-enumeration measure so a non-owner cannot distinguish "does not exist" from "exists but is private".

parameters.name: uuid
parameters.description: The UUID v4 identifier of the QR code, returned by the generate endpoint

200.description: QR code file

404.description: QR code not found - either the UUID is unknown/soft-deleted, the file is no longer present on disk, OR (see the owner-or-public rule above) the caller is not the owner of a private claimed code. All three cases return this identical shape by design.

value.message: QR code not found.

owner_mismatch.summary: Private claimed code owned by someone else (anti-enumeration: identical to not_found)

value.message: QR code not found.

file_not_found.summary: Record exists but the underlying file is no longer present on disk

value.message: This QR code's file is no longer available for download.

get.description: Check the health status of the API. Returns database connectivity, application version, and PHP version. Used by monitoring systems and load balancers. No authentication required. This route IS subject to the same per-IP rate limiting as every other endpoint (no special-case exemption in the router) - monitoring/load-balancer callers should poll no more frequently than the advertised `X-RateLimit-Limit`.

200.description: Service is healthy

value.message: Service is healthy.
Service is degraded.

post.description: Create a new (pending) user account and queue an email-verification message. ANTI-ENUMERATION: this endpoint ALWAYS returns the same 201 response, whether the email address was brand new or already registered - the caller cannot distinguish the two outcomes. No new verification email is sent for an already-registered address. Requires a valid CSRF token (web UI) or API key.

201.description: Registration request accepted (identical response regardless of whether the email was new or already registered)

value.message: If this email address is available for registration, a verification link has been sent to it.

post.summary: Log in and establish a session
post.description: Authenticate by email + password and, on success, issue a database-backed session (tblUserSessions) and regenerate the PHP session id. ANTI-ENUMERATION: every failure path (wrong password, no such account, locked account, unverified/pending account, suspended account) returns the IDENTICAL 401 response - none of these states are distinguishable from the outside. Failed attempts count towards an account lockout (security.max_login_attempts, default 5 / security.lockout_duration, default 900 seconds / 15 minutes - both configurable server settings). Requires a valid CSRF token (web UI) or API key. NOTE: the session itself is established purely via a `Set-Cookie` response header (PHP's native session cookie, rotated via `session_regenerate_id()`) - it is NOT returned as a field in the JSON body; subsequent same-origin requests rely on the browser resending that cookie automatically.

200.description: Login successful - a session has been established

value.message: Logged in successfully.

401.description: Invalid email or password, or the account is not yet verified (a single generic message covers every failure mode - see description above)

value.message: Invalid email or password, or the account is not yet verified.

post.description: Revoke the current database-backed session (if any) and rotate the PHP session id. Idempotent - calling this with no active session is a harmless no-op that still returns 200, so a status-code difference can never be used to probe session state. Requires a valid CSRF token (web UI) or API key.

200.description: Logged out (idempotent - returned even if there was no active session)

value.message: Logged out successfully.

post.description: Consume a single-use, expiring email-verification token (from the link emailed by POST /auth/register) and activate the owning account. Requires a valid CSRF token (web UI) or API key.

200.description: Email address verified; the account is now active

value.message: Your email address has been verified. You can now log in.

400.description: The token is invalid, not found, or has expired

value.message: This verification link is invalid or has expired.

post.description: Queue a password-reset email if (and only if) the address belongs to an active account. ANTI-ENUMERATION: ALWAYS returns the IDENTICAL 200 response regardless of whether the email is registered - this is a hard requirement (SECURITY.md), not an implementation detail. Requires a valid CSRF token (web UI) or API key.

200.description: Request accepted (identical response regardless of whether the email is registered)

value.message: If this email address is registered, a password reset link has been sent to it.

post.summary: Reset a password using an emailed token
post.description: Consume a single-use, expiring password-reset token (from the link emailed by POST /auth/request-password-reset) and set a new password. All existing sessions for the account are revoked on success. Requires a valid CSRF token (web UI) or API key.

200.description: Password reset - all existing sessions for the account have been revoked

value.message: Your password has been reset. You can now log in with your new password.

400.description: Missing fields, or the token is invalid/not found/expired

value.message: This password reset link is invalid or has expired.

post.summary: Save a generated QR code to your account
post.description: Claim a previously-generated QR code (by the `uuid` returned from POST /generate) into the authenticated caller's account, or - if the caller already owns it - update its label/visibility. Enforces the caller's plan `saved_codes` limit (`-1` = unlimited) ONLY for a genuinely NEW claim; re-saving an already-owned code never consumes a fresh slot. A code already claimed by a DIFFERENT user is reported as `404` (never `403`/`409` at this stage) to avoid disclosing that the UUID belongs to somebody else. Requires a valid CSRF token (web UI) or API key belonging to an authenticated account. requiredScope: `save` (API-key requests only; session/CSRF requests are never scope-limited).

200.description: An already-owned code's label/visibility was updated

201.description: The code was newly claimed into the caller's account

value.message: QR code saved to your account.

404.description: The UUID does not exist, has been deleted, or is already saved to a DIFFERENT account (indistinguishable from not-found - see description above)

value.message: QR code not found.

409.description: Lost a race to a concurrent claim of the same code

429.description: Too many requests. Two distinct causes share this status code on `/save` specifically: (1) the router's generic per-key/per-IP rate limit (`RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`), or (2) `SAVE_LOCK_BUSY` - the per-user `saved_codes` advisory lock (SECURITY.md F-023, closing a plan-limit TOCTOU race) timed out because another `/save` request for this SAME account is already mid-flight. Both include a `Retry-After` header; back off and retry.

value.message: Rate limit exceeded. Please wait before making another request.
The saved-codes service is busy processing another request for your account. Please try again shortly.

500.description: The claim/update database write failed unexpectedly (error_code SAVE_FAILED)

value.message: Failed to save this QR code. Please try again.

get.description: Lists ONLY the authenticated caller's own saved QR codes - never another user's rows, public or otherwise. Supports pagination (`page`, `per_page`, capped at 100) and an optional `type` filter matching the QR code type name. requiredScope: `qrcodes:read` (API-key requests only; session/CSRF requests are never scope-limited).

parameters.description: 1-based page number (default 1; clamped up to 1 if lower)

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Filter to a single QR code type name (e.g. "url", "wifi")

200.description: The caller's saved QR codes, paginated

get.description: Allowed only if the caller owns the code OR it is marked `is_public: true` - otherwise `404` (never `403`, to avoid disclosing that a private UUID belonging to someone else exists). requiredScope: `qrcodes:read` (API-key requests only; session/CSRF requests are never scope-limited).

parameters.name: uuid
parameters.description: The UUID v4 identifier of the saved QR code

200.description: The QR code (caller owns it, or it is public)

404.description: Not found, deleted, or not owned-and-not-public (identical response for all three - see description above)

value.message: QR code not found.

patch.summary: Update a saved QR code you own
patch.description: Update the `label`, `is_public` visibility, and/or visual `customization` of a saved code the caller OWNS. Ownership is checked BEFORE any other field is read - a non-owned code (including a PUBLIC one; `is_public` never grants write access) is reported as `404`. When `customization` is supplied, the QR image is regenerated in place from the code's existing payload (its `download_url`/`uuid` do not change) and `qrFilePath`/`qrOptions`/`qrOutputFormat` are updated. Content/destination changes are out of scope for this stage. requiredScope: `qrcodes:write` (API-key requests only; session/CSRF requests are never scope-limited).

parameters.name: uuid
parameters.description: The UUID v4 identifier of the saved QR code

200.description: The saved QR code was updated

404.description: Not owned by the caller (or does not exist / was deleted) - identical response either way

500.description: The regeneration engine, or the ensuing database write, failed unexpectedly (error_code FILE_SAVE_FAILED or UPDATE_FAILED)

delete.summary: Delete a saved QR code you own
delete.description: Soft-deletes (sets `deletedAt`; the row is retained for audit purposes) a saved code the caller OWNS, freeing one `saved_codes` plan slot. Ownership is checked before any mutation; a non-owned code is reported as `404`. requiredScope: `qrcodes:write` (API-key requests only; session/CSRF requests are never scope-limited).

parameters.name: uuid
parameters.description: The UUID v4 identifier of the saved QR code

200.description: The saved QR code was deleted

value.message: QR code deleted successfully.

404.description: Not owned by the caller (or does not exist / already deleted) - identical response either way

500.description: The database delete failed unexpectedly (error_code DELETE_FAILED)

patch.summary: Update your own display name and/or avatar
patch.description: Own-account only - the caller's identity is resolved server-side from the CSRF session context, never from a request field. Accepts any combination of display_name, avatar_base64, and remove_avatar (see AccountProfileUpdateRequest). **F-026: session-only.** Account management is reserved for an interactive (CSRF/session) caller - an X-API-Key-authenticated request gets `403 ACCOUNT_MANAGEMENT_FORBIDDEN` regardless of that key's scopes (API keys are for programmatic QR operations only, never account control).

200.description: Profile updated successfully

value.message: Profile updated successfully.

403.description: Authenticated via X-API-Key rather than CSRF/session - account management is CSRF/session-only (F-026)

account_management_forbidden.summary: API-key auth cannot manage the account

value.message: Account management requires an interactive session; API keys cannot manage the account.

500.description: The profile/avatar database write, or avatar file save/removal, failed unexpectedly (error_code UPDATE_FAILED, AVATAR_SAVE_FAILED, or AVATAR_REMOVE_FAILED)

get.summary: List ONLY your own active sessions
get.description: Returns every non-revoked, non-expired tblUserSessions row owned by the caller - the WHERE clause is unconditionally scoped to the caller's own userID; there is no parameter that widens this to another user's sessions. **F-026: session-only.** Account management is reserved for an interactive (CSRF/session) caller - an X-API-Key-authenticated request gets `403 ACCOUNT_MANAGEMENT_FORBIDDEN` regardless of that key's scopes (API keys are for programmatic QR operations only, never account control).

200.description: Sessions retrieved successfully

403.description: Authenticated via X-API-Key rather than CSRF/session - account management is CSRF/session-only (F-026)

account_management_forbidden.summary: API-key auth cannot manage the account

value.message: Account management requires an interactive session; API keys cannot manage the account.

post.summary: Permanently erase your OWN account by anonymization (GDPR/CCPA, #37)
post.description: Erases the caller's OWN account by ANONYMIZATION, never a hard delete of the row: `email` is replaced with a non-reversible `deleted-<userID>@deleted.invalid` placeholder, `displayName` becomes 'Deleted user', `firstName`/`lastName`/`avatarPath` are cleared (the avatar FILE is also deleted), `passwordHash` is cleared (login becomes impossible), and `status` becomes 'deleted' with `erasedAt` set. Subscription/payment rows are RETAINED (for financial/audit obligations) but carry no PII beyond the now-anonymized account reference. Requires the caller's CURRENT password (wrong password -> `401 INVALID_PASSWORD`, nothing is mutated) and an explicit `"confirm": true` in the request body (`400 CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` otherwise). Ends the session on success. **F-026 pattern: session-only.** Account management is reserved for an interactive (CSRF/session) caller - an X-API-Key-authenticated request gets `403 ACCOUNT_MANAGEMENT_FORBIDDEN` regardless of that key's scopes.

get.summary: Begin an SSO sign-in/link attempt (BROWSER REDIRECT, not JSON)
get.description: ⚠️ NOT a JSON API endpoint - this is a browser-redirect route (Epic E2, #55/#19/#20/#28), documented here for completeness only. A visitor's browser navigates here directly (an <a href> on the login/register page for an anonymous sign-in); the response is an HTTP 302 redirect to the provider's own authorize URL (PKCE S256 challenge + a fresh `state`/`nonce` bound to the visitor's session), never a JSON body. If the visitor is ALREADY authenticated, a bare GET instead renders a one-click HTML confirmation page containing the CSRF-protected POST form that actually begins the "link an additional provider" flow (see the POST variant below) - a link never begins from a bare GET with no CSRF token. Renders an accessible HTML error page (not JSON) if the provider is unknown or not currently enabled+configured (ssoProviderIsUsable()).

parameters.description: Optional post-login destination - MUST be a same-site, root-relative path (validated against an allowlist via resolveSafeSameSiteRedirect(); an absolute URL, protocol-relative //host, or a javascript:/other scheme silently falls back to /account/)

post.summary: Begin a "link an additional provider" attempt (authenticated, CSRF-protected, BROWSER REDIRECT)
post.description: ⚠️ NOT a JSON API endpoint. Used by the account-settings "Link ..." buttons (public_html/account/index.php), which render this as a real <form method="POST"> with a CSRF token - required because, unlike the anonymous GET sign-in flow above, this action affects an ALREADY-authenticated account (Epic E2's "CSRF on the initiation" requirement). On success, 302-redirects to the provider's authorize URL exactly like the GET variant; the CALLBACK then links the verified identity onto the CURRENTLY authenticated account rather than creating/logging into a different one - see decideOAuthAccountLinkAction().

get.description: ⚠️ NOT a JSON API endpoint - documented here for completeness only. This is the provider's own redirect back to this app after the visitor authenticates/consents (or declines). Verifies `state` (CSRF/replay defence, single-use), exchanges `code` + the PKCE `code_verifier` for tokens at the provider's token endpoint (≤10s), cryptographically verifies the `id_token` (JWKS fetch+cache, RS256-only signature check via openssl_verify(), then iss/aud/exp/iat/nonce claim validation), then applies the account-linking decision table (create a pre-verified account / log an existing linked user in / link an additional provider onto the CURRENTLY authenticated account / refuse - see decideOAuthAccountLinkAction()'s full rationale). On a genuine sign-in outcome, issues a normal CueRCode session via the same hardened path every other login uses (PHP session ID regenerated - session-fixation mitigation). Responds with an HTTP 302 redirect to the caller's (re-validated, same-site-only) safe post-login destination on success, or an accessible HTML error page on any failure - NEVER a JSON body, and no internal error detail beyond a safe generic message.

parameters.description: The authorization code issued by the provider (absent when `error` is present instead)

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: The state value round-tripped from the initiation request - verified against the session-bound value (single-use; burned on read regardless of outcome)

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: Set by the IdP itself when the visitor cancelled consent or the IdP encountered its own error (e.g. access_denied) - when present, code/state are not processed at all

302.description: Sign-in/link completed - redirecting to the caller's safe post-login destination

200.description: An accessible HTML error page - invalid/expired/replayed state, failed token exchange, failed id_token verification (bad iss/aud/exp/nonce/signature), unverified-email refusal (SSO_EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED), email-collision refusal (SSO_EMAIL_COLLISION - requires manual link), provider-already-linked-to-a-different-account refusal (SSO_ALREADY_LINKED_ELSEWHERE), or an IdP-reported error/cancellation

type.description: The QR code type identifier (one of 26 supported types). Use the /types endpoint to retrieve the definitive active list and each type's form field schema. Maximum 64 characters.

input.description: Type-specific input data. The required fields depend on the QR code type; use /types to obtain the form schema for each type. Each scalar field is limited to 4096 characters. Examples: url -> {"url":"https://example.com"}; wifi -> {"ssid":"...","password":"...","encryption":"WPA","hidden":false}; vcard -> {"first_name":"John","last_name":"Doe",...}; geo -> {"latitude":51.5074,"longitude":-0.1278,"label":"London"}; gs1_product -> {"gtin":"09521234543213","batch":"LOT42"}.

Customization.description: Visual customisation options for the QR code. All fields are optional; defaults are applied for missing values. The same object is accepted at the request level for bulk generation (as shared defaults) and per item/row (overriding the shared defaults key-by-key). Unknown keys are ignored.

format.description: Output image format. `jpeg` is an accepted alias of `jpg`. Note: JPEG-XL (`jxl`) is NOT accepted on this host (see the API description); an unrecognised value falls back to `png`.

size.description: Target image size in pixels (width/height). Clamped to the 100-4000 range server-side. Ignored by /preview (always 300px).

ecc.description: Error correction level. L=7%, M=15%, Q=25%, H=30% recovery. Higher levels tolerate more damage/obstruction. The API default is M (the web UI defaults to H). Use H when adding a logo.

fg_color.description: Foreground (dark module) colour as a hex code (#RGB, #RRGGBB, or #RRGGBBAA).

bg_color.description: Background (light module) colour as a hex code.

marker_color.description: Finder pattern (corner squares) colour as a hex code. Optional; defaults to the foreground colour when omitted or empty.

pattern.description: Module (pixel) shape style. Only square/round/dot are accepted; any other value is silently coerced to square by the server.

oneOf.description: Predefined logo ID from the logo library (tblPredefinedLogos).
`upload` to use a custom logo supplied via logo_data, or a logo identifier/path.

logo.description: Logo to overlay on the QR code centre. Using a logo automatically upgrades ECC to H. Set to `upload` and provide logo_data + logo_mime for a custom image.

logo_data.description: Base64-encoded custom logo as a data URI (e.g. `data:image/png;base64,...`). Used only when `logo` is `upload`.

logo_mime.description: MIME type of the uploaded custom logo. Used only when `logo` is `upload`. An `image/svg+xml` logo is additionally scanned server-side and rejected with 422 LOGO_SVG_REJECTED if it contains active content (e.g. <script>, event handler attributes, external references).

logo_size_pct.description: Logo size as a percentage of the QR code dimensions. Clamped server-side to 5-40 (matches the UI slider's range).

frame_style.description: Decorative frame style drawn around the QR code. Label/banner/pill styles render the frame_label text. Not applied to PDF output. NOTE: unlike the other enum fields in this schema, an out-of-enum value is not rejected by a dedicated allowlist at the request-parsing layer; behaviour for an unrecognised string is delegated to the frame-rendering engine.

frame_label.description: Text label for label/banner/pill frame styles (e.g. 'SCAN ME'). Maximum 120 characters (the UI limits this to 30).

frame_color.description: Frame border/background colour as a hex code.

transparent.description: Whether the background should be transparent. Honoured for PNG, GIF, WebP, and SVG; ignored for JPEG and PDF.

quiet_zone.description: Whether to include the quiet zone (the white margin around the QR code) that improves scanning reliability.

version.description: Optional fixed QR code version (1-40) controlling the module grid size (modules = 4 * version + 17). When omitted, the smallest version that fits the payload at the chosen ECC level is selected automatically.

preset.description: Customisation preset. `none` (default) applies no additional rules. `accessible` enforces an accessibility-focused configuration per ISO/IEC 18004 + WCAG 2.1: forces `ecc` to `H`, forces `quiet_zone` to `true`, DROPS any pinned `version` so the smallest auto-fit version is used, and evaluates the WCAG contrast ratio of `fg_color`/`bg_color`. A contrast ratio below 3:1 causes the request to be REJECTED with HTTP 422 (error_code `ACCESSIBLE_CONTRAST_TOO_LOW`); a ratio from 3:1 up to (but not including) 4.5:1 is allowed through but reported as a non-blocking warning in the response `data.metadata.contrast_warning` field. See the /generate 422 response for a worked example.

scan_distance_cm.description: Optional intended scanning distance in centimetres, used only to compute a recommended physical print size via the 10:1 scan-distance rule (recommended size ≈ scan distance / 10, with a 20mm practical floor). When supplied together with `preset: accessible`, the recommendation is returned in the response as `data.metadata.recommended_print_size_mm`. Has no effect on the generated image itself.

gradient.description: Gradient fill for the dark modules (SVG output only). Advanced feature; not exposed in the standard web UI. Ignored for non-SVG formats.

pdf_layout.description: Print layout for `format: pdf` (E5 / #49). Ignored for any other format. `standard` (default) is today's unchanged QR-only PDF, byte-for-byte. `accessible_caption` adds a large-print (>=18pt) human-readable caption plus a Grade-1 (uncontracted) Braille caption line, rendered as geometric dot patterns (not a Unicode Braille font - core PDF fonts have no Braille glyphs). `tactile` includes everything in `accessible_caption` PLUS a second, clearly-delineated page containing CueRCode's own tactile locator frame overlay guide (registration marks + orientation dot), meant to be reproduced via swell paper, a Braille embosser, or a UV-varnish/raised-ink pass aligned with page 1 - this is an original design, not a reproduction of any third-party patented locator. `avery_5160` (US Letter, 3x10) and `avery_l7160` (A4, 3x7) tile the code into an Avery address-label sheet; on `/generate` a single code fills exactly ONE label with the rest of the sheet left blank as a printable template, while `/bulk-generate` (see BulkGenerateRequest) tiles MULTIPLE items across successive labels/pages when the SAME `pdf_layout` is set at the request level. See `/accessibility` on the web UI for the print/embossing best-practice guide.

image.description: Base64 data URI of the generated QR code image

download_url.description: Relative URL for downloading the QR code file

mime_type.description: MIME type of the generated image

image.description: Base64 data URI of the preview image (always PNG, 300px)

AccessibleMetadata.description: Present in /generate and /preview responses ONLY when the request's customization.preset was 'accessible' (E5 / #48). Absent entirely for preset=none (the default).

accessible.description: Always true when this object is present.

contrast_ratio.description: The WCAG contrast ratio computed between fg_color and bg_color, rounded to 2 decimal places. Range 1.0-21.0.

contrast_warning.description: Present ONLY when 3:1 <= contrast_ratio < 4.5:1 - a non-blocking accessibility warning (requests below 3:1 are rejected with HTTP 422 instead; see the /generate 422 response).
contrast_warning.example: Contrast ratio 3.5:1 is below the recommended WCAG AA level of 4.5:1. Consider a higher-contrast colour pair for maximum readability.

recommended_print_size_mm.description: Recommended minimum print size (width = height) in millimetres, computed from the request's scan_distance_cm via the 10:1 scan-distance rule (20mm practical floor). Null when scan_distance_cm was not supplied.

count.description: Total number of active QR code types

name.description: Type identifier (use this in the 'type' field of generate/preview requests)

icon.description: FontAwesome icon class for UI rendering

description.description: Brief description of the QR code type
description.example: Open a website or web page

form_fields.description: Form field schema defining the input fields for this type (name, label, type, required, validation, etc.)

payload_template.description: Template showing the generated payload format, or null when the type is built by a dedicated payload builder.

description.example: PNG image (lossless compression, transparent background support)

supports_transparency.description: Whether the format supports transparent backgrounds

supports_logo.description: Whether the format supports logo overlay

supports_frame.description: Whether the format supports frame rendering

error_code.description: Machine-readable error code for programmatic handling. Known codes include: MISSING_FIELD, FIELD_TOO_LONG, INVALID_JSON, INVALID_CUSTOMIZATION, UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE, PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, GENERATION_FAILED, LOGO_SVG_REJECTED, AUTH_REQUIRED, INVALID_API_KEY, INVALID_CSRF_TOKEN, NOT_FOUND, ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND, METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED, RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, FETCH_ERROR, LOOKUP_ERROR, FILE_NOT_FOUND, SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, ZIP_UNAVAILABLE, BULK_NO_INPUT, BULK_INVALID_BODY, BULK_INVALID_ITEMS, BULK_EMPTY, BULK_INVALID_ITEM, BULK_INVALID_CSV, BULK_CSV_NO_HEADER, BULK_CSV_NO_TYPE, BULK_CSV_NO_INPUT, BULK_ITEM_MISSING_TYPE, BULK_ITEM_MISSING_INPUT, BULK_TOO_MANY_ITEMS, BULK_TEMP_FAILED, BULK_ZIP_FAILED, BULK_READ_FAILED, INVALID_EMAIL, WEAK_PASSWORD, INVALID_CREDENTIALS, VERIFICATION_TOKEN_INVALID, VERIFICATION_ALREADY_USED, RESET_TOKEN_INVALID, RESET_TOKEN_ALREADY_USED, CSRF_INVALID, HASH_FAILED, ACTIVATION_FAILED, RESET_FAILED, INVALID_UUID, INVALID_LABEL, NO_FIELDS, SAVED_CODES_LIMIT_REACHED, SAVE_CONFLICT, SAVE_FAILED, LIST_FAILED, UPDATE_FAILED, DELETE_FAILED, REGENERATION_FAILED, FILE_SAVE_FAILED, ACCESSIBLE_CONTRAST_TOO_LOW, SAVE_LOCK_BUSY, INVALID_AVATAR, AVATAR_SAVE_FAILED, AVATAR_REMOVE_FAILED, INVALID_CURRENT_PASSWORD, INVALID_PASSWORD, INVALID_REQUEST, CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED, ALREADY_ERASED, ERASE_FAILED, ACCOUNT_MANAGEMENT_FORBIDDEN, LOOKUP_FAILED, INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE, API_KEY_MANAGEMENT_FORBIDDEN, API_KEY_LIMIT_REACHED, INVALID_SCOPE, CREATE_FAILED, ROTATE_FAILED.

password.description: Minimum length defaults to 8 (the `password_min_length` server setting may raise this floor - 8 is a default, not a hard-coded minimum) and is also checked against a common-password denylist and a single-repeated-character rejection; violations return 422 WEAK_PASSWORD.

token.description: The raw token from the emailed verification link
The raw token from the emailed reset link

new_password.description: Minimum length defaults to 8 (the `password_min_length` server setting may raise this floor) and is also checked against a common-password denylist and a single-repeated-character rejection; violations return 422 WEAK_PASSWORD.
new_password.example: a new correct horse battery staple

AuthGenericResponse.description: Generic success envelope used by every account/auth endpoint below. register/request-password-reset deliberately return an IDENTICAL shape regardless of whether the target account exists (anti user-enumeration, see SECURITY.md).

message.example: If this email address is available for registration, a verification link has been sent to it.

uuid.description: The UUID returned by a prior POST /generate call

label.description: Caller-supplied nickname for this saved code. Omit to leave unchanged; an explicit empty string or null clears it.

is_public.description: Opt-in: when true, this code becomes readable/downloadable by ANY authenticated caller, not just the owner. Defaults to false (private) for a NEW claim; omitted on an already-owned code leaves its current visibility unchanged.

message.example: QR code saved to your account.

QrCodeSummary.description: One saved QR code as returned by GET /qrcodes and GET /qrcodes/{uuid}. Never includes the owner's userID/email - a public code viewed by a non-owner must not disclose who owns it.

PatchQrCodeRequest.description: All fields optional, but at least one of label/is_public/customization must be present (else 400 NO_FIELDS). "customization" fields omitted from a partial update inherit the code's EXISTING stored value.

AccountProfileUpdateRequest.description: At least one of display_name, avatar_base64, or remove_avatar must be supplied. avatar_base64 and remove_avatar are mutually exclusive in effect (an upload takes precedence if both are somehow sent).

avatar_base64.description: A 'data:image/{png,jpeg,gif,webp};base64,...' data URI. SVG is explicitly rejected for avatars (self-stored-XSS mitigation - see fn_api_account.php).

remove_avatar.description: Set true to clear the current custom avatar.

new_password.description: Minimum length defaults to 8 (the `password_min_length` server setting may raise this floor) and is also checked against a common-password denylist and a single-repeated-character rejection; violations return 422 WEAK_PASSWORD.

id.description: The full session identifier - pass this to DELETE /account/sessions/{id} to revoke it.

masked_id.description: The SAME identifier, masked for display (all but the trailing 8 characters).

is_current.description: True if this row is the session making THIS request.

current_password.description: The caller's CURRENT password - re-verified server-side (wrong -> 401 INVALID_PASSWORD, nothing is mutated). IMPORTANT: an account that signed up via SSO only (no local password ever set) can NEVER supply a matching current_password and therefore cannot self-erase through this endpoint at all - every attempt returns 401 INVALID_PASSWORD.

confirm.description: Must be the literal boolean true - anything else (absent, "true" string, 1, false) fails closed with 400 CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED.

message.example: Your account has been erased. You have been signed out.

erased_at.description: The UTC timestamp the anonymization transaction committed, formatted as `Y-m-d H:i:s` (space-separated, NOT RFC3339/ISO-8601 - unlike `AccountDataExportResponse.data.exported_at`, which IS ISO-8601). e.g. '2026-07-10 19:12:58'.

has_custom_avatar.description: True if a custom avatar file is set - the file itself is fetched separately via the session-gated /account/avatar/ endpoint, never embedded here.

payload.description: The raw, already-encoded QR payload string - never the rendered image blob.

input_data.description: The original form field values behind the payload, when captured.

customization.description: The visual customisation snapshot (colours, size, ECC, frame, etc.) used at generation time.

masked_id.description: The session identifier, masked for display - the raw, replayable token is never included in an export.

masked_subject.description: The provider subject identifier, masked - never the tokensEncrypted bundle.

message.example: Your account data export is ready.

profile.description: null if the profile row could not be looked up (e.g. a transient database error during export assembly); otherwise always populated for an existing account.

name.description: A caller-chosen label to tell your keys apart (matches tblAPIKeys.apiKeyName VARCHAR(100)).

scopes.description: Scopes to grant this key, from the allowlist. Omitted/empty means the key is granted NO scopes (it can authenticate but cannot access any scoped endpoint).

ApiKeySecretResponse.description: The ONE-TIME response shape returned by POST /keys (create) and POST /keys/{id}/rotate - `data.api_key` is the ONLY time the full raw key is ever returned; it cannot be retrieved again afterward (only its hash is stored).

message.example: API key created. Copy it now - it will not be shown again.

id.description: The tblAPIKeys.apiKeyID - pass this to POST /keys/{id}/rotate or DELETE /keys/{id}.

api_key.description: The FULL raw API key. Shown ONLY here, ONLY ONCE - copy it now.

prefix.description: The same key's first 12 characters, for identification in the dashboard list (this alone is NOT a usable credential).

scopes.description: Present on CREATE only (rotate preserves the existing scopes without re-stating them in the response).

rate_limits.description: Present on CREATE only. Derived from the owning user's CURRENT plan at creation time.

last_used_at.description: Present on CREATE only - always null for a brand-new key.

expires_at.description: Present on CREATE only. Self-service creation does not currently expose an expiry input (always null); the column IS enforced server-side if ever set another way.

ApiKeyInfo.description: One item in GET /keys' list - NEVER includes the full key or its hash.

is_active.description: false = revoked (soft-deleted). Revoked keys remain in this list for audit purposes.
